en: The Apadāna of the Elder Madhumaṁsadāyaka Bhaddāli-vagga, Chapter 4, Number 4 [Verse 1] "I was a king named Mahinda, ruling over the earth. I gave a gift of honey and meat to the Buddha Kassapa. [Verse 2] "Because of that root of merit, for ninety-one eons I did not fall into the states of misery; I was reborn in heaven. [Verse 3] "For eighty-four thousand eons I dwelt in the world of the gods, And for eighty-four thousand eons I dwelt among humans. [Verse 4] "In my final existence, I was born into a wealthy family; I was handsome, possessed of great beauty, and endowed with splendor. [Verse 5] "When I was sixteen years of age, I went forth into homelessness; Having become a monk, I attained the state of an arahant. [Verse 6] "The Teacher, the Great Sage, the Fully Enlightened One, Taught me the Dhamma;

having heard it, I attained the fruit of arahantship. [Verse 7] "Today I have attained the goal, and all suffering has been destroyed; I am free from birth and death, having reached the end of the cycle of rebirth. [Verse 8] "I have lived the holy life; there is nothing more to do; I have laid down this burden and achieved my own goal. [Verse 9] "Having heard the teaching of the Teacher, the Fully Enlightened One, I have attained the supreme peace, the coolness of Nibbāna. [Verse 10] "This is my final body; I shall never again be subject to birth; I have crossed over the ocean of saṃsāra and reached the further shore. [Verse 11] "By giving honey and meat to the Buddha Kassapa, I have attained the supreme fruit, the state of an arahant. [Verse 12] "May all beings who hear this account of the Elder Madhumaṁsadāyaka Be established in the Three Refuges and attain the fruit of stream-entry. [Verse 13] "May they be freed from all suffering and attain the bliss of Nibbāna; May they be established in the True Dhamma and reach the end of suffering. [Verse 14] "May the merit gained by reciting this Apadāna Cause all beings to cross over the flood of saṃsāra. [Verse 15] "May the Elder Madhumaṁsadāyaka, having fulfilled his duties, Attain Parinibbāna, like a lamp going out. [Verse 16] "Thus did the Elder Madhumaṁsadāyaka speak these verses; Having attained the goal, he passed away into Nibbāna. [Verse 17] "Thus ends the Apadāna of the Elder Madhumaṁsadāyaka, The fourth discourse in the Bhaddāli-vagga."
“In the city of Bandhumatī,
I was a pork-butcher;
having boiled a pig’s trotter, I sold it.”
I sprinkled honey and meat [over it].
Having gone to the assembly,
I took up a single bowl.
Having filled that bowl,
I gave it to the community of monks. Therein,
whichever monk was the most senior elder—
He then presented me with it;
by means of this bowlful,
may you obtain abundant happiness.
Having enjoyed two kinds of prosperity,
urged on by the root of merit,
while the final [age] was proceeding—
He will burn away the defilements.
Having gladdened my mind therein,
I went to the realm of the Thirty-three.
Having eaten and drunk there,
I obtain abundant happiness,
whether in a pavilion or at the foot of a tree.
I recollected my past deeds;
a rain of food and drink fell upon me,
raining down for that entire time.
This is my final one;
my last existence is now proceeding.
Even here, food and drink for me—
It rains at all times.
Because of that very gift of honey,
having wandered through existence, I—
Having fully understood all taints,
I dwell free from taints.
Ninety-one aeons ago...
Because I gave that gift at that time,
I do not know a state of misery;
this is the fruit of the gift of honey.
The defilements have been burnt away by me;
I dwell free from taints.
Welcome indeed has come to me...
[and so on] ...the Buddha’s instruction has been fulfilled.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so on]...
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Madhumamsadāyaka spoke these verses.
This is the fourth legend of the elder Madhumamsadāyaka.
